what_taken: Nonlinear optimisation (R, solnp) of national diets for 152 countries, 2011 intake of 221 foods, minimising relative departure from the observed diet under 29 nutrient limits, five per-capita planetary-boundary limits and four acceptability rules (p.7694, 7696). Observed diets sit inside the carbon limit in 85 countries; optimised diets sit inside all five limits in all 152 (p.7698). Carbon and nitrogen limits are hardest to meet (p.7700).

what_taken: Narrative review of 67 diet-optimisation studies (abstract). Covers objectives (minimum cost, least departure from the observed diet) and nutrient, cost, cultural and environmental constraints. A constraint that cannot be met signals clashing nutrient recommendations, monotonous eating patterns, too few nutrient-rich foods, or a clash with another dimension (abstract). Nutrition, cost and environment read as compatible up to a 30 to 40% cut in diet impact (section Designing sustainable diets).

what_taken: 9,341 Australian adult daily diets from the Australian Health Survey 2011-12, each scored on climate, water-scarcity and cropland-scarcity footprints, merged into one score weighted by distance to planetary-boundary targets, and on diet quality against the Australian Dietary Guidelines (p.803-805). A guideline diet built from lower-impact eating patterns cut the score 15.9% and the climate footprint 34.9% but raised the water-scarcity footprint 11.6%; no footprint reached its target (p.806).

what_taken: LUTO, a constrained partial-equilibrium linear-programming land-use model of Australia (24 land uses, 1.1 km grid), run on 648 pathways to 2050 against seven land-sector targets at three ambition levels, targets set from a 2012 baseline (p.217-218). Moderate 2030 water target (no more than 5,783 GL a year in water-stressed catchments) met in 41.7% of pathways; two targets together in 24.5%, five together in 0.9% (p.219).

Conclusion on p.221 recommends pairing land system models such as LUTO with models of energy, climate, economy, resource use and population.

what_taken: FABLE Calculator, an Excel model of the Australian food and land system (2000 to 2050, 5-year steps, 2010 base, no optimisation), run as 200,000 Monte Carlo scenarios across SSP1, SSP2 and SSP3 ranges against five environmental targets plus exports (Methods, Results). All met with exports at 1.5 times 2010 or more: 13% of SSP1 scenarios, none of SSP2 or SSP3 (Results; abstract says about 10%).

what_taken: Compares four World3-03 scenarios (BAU, BAU2, CT, SW) with observed world data for 10 variables, final data years 2015 to 2020, using value difference, rate-of-change difference and normalised root mean square difference with 20%, 50% and 20% tolerances (p.617-619). Closest-fit counts: CT 7, BAU2 6, BAU 4, SW 3, none 2 (Table 3, p.622). BAU is not the closest fit, which differs from Turner's comparisons (p.623).

what_taken: Review of water resources carrying capacity methods, five in all: conventional trend, system dynamics (stock, flow, feedback, delay), multi-objective model analysis, comprehensive evaluation and dynamic simulation recursive (p.455-458). Indices and weights in the multi-objective and comprehensive-evaluation methods are set by the researchers; dynamic simulation recursive is described as closest to the physical meaning of carrying capacity and needs long, high-quality series (p.457-458). The paper gives no capacity values.

what_taken: Shocks (production drops found as residual outliers against a 7-year median baseline) in 741 national series for crops, livestock, fisheries and aquaculture, 1961 to 2013: 226 shocks in 134 nations (p.130, 135). Decade averages of shock frequency rise in all four sectors (p.130). Extreme weather caused over half of crop shocks; geopolitical events 41% of livestock shocks (p.131). National totals smooth out shocks in large countries such as Australia (p.135).

what_taken: Principal component analysis (varimax rotation) of FAO food balance sheet energy shares for 18 food groups in 171 countries, 1961 to 2013. Four scores explain 89.2% of variance: animal source and sugar; vegetable; starchy root and fruit; seafood and oilcrops (file p.4, 14). It describes change in supply composition, comparing 1961-65 with 2009-13; Australia is among the high-income English-speaking countries whose animal source and sugar score fell most (file p.7).
